verbalization: The visible evidence suggests a potential relationship between quillaic acid alpha-L-Arap-(1->4)-alpha-L-Arap-(1->3)-beta-D-Xylp-(1->4)-alpha-L-Rhap-(1->2)-beta-D-fucopyranosyl ester and Histone-lysine N-methyltransferase, H3 lysine-9 specific 5, through a series of molecular interactions. This compound is identified as a target of two different compounds: (+)-Phylliroside and Dimethyl 3-hydroxyphthalate, both of which are linked to the EZH2/SUZ12/EED complex. The EZH2/SUZ12/EED complex is known to be a key component of the polycomb repressive complex 2 (PRC2), which is involved in the methylation of histone lysine residues, particularly lysine 9 of histone H3 (H3K9me). The evidence suggests that the quillaic acid compound may act as a modulator or inhibitor of this complex, thereby influencing the activity of the histone methyltransferase enzyme. The shared target of these compounds and the involvement of the EZH2/SUZ12/EED complex in histone methylation provide a plausible mechanism for the observed relationship. However, the exact nature of the interaction and the specific molecular pathways involved remain to be fully elucidated.
